topic.seo_intro:
BRCA2 is a tumor suppressor gene that plays a critical role in DNA repair and cancer prevention. When inherited mutations occur in the BRCA2 gene, individuals face significantly elevated risks for developing breast cancer, ovarian cancer, and several other malignancies. Understanding BRCA2 has revolutionized cancer diagnostics and personalized treatment strategies, offering patients and families the opportunity for earlier detection and tailored therapeutic approaches.

Research into BRCA2 continues to advance rapidly, with scientists working to improve genetic testing accuracy, develop targeted therapies for BRCA2-mutated cancers, and enhance risk assessment for affected families. Recent studies have revealed new insights into how BRCA2 mutations influence cancer development and how emerging treatments like PARP inhibitors can specifically target these genetic vulnerabilities. This knowledge is transforming clinical practice and improving outcomes for individuals with BRCA2-related cancers.

On this page, you'll find comprehensive information about BRCA2 as a biomarker and diagnostic tool in cancer research. We've curated the latest peer-reviewed studies and clinical findings to help patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals understand current advances in BRCA2 testing, risk stratification, and evidence-based treatment options. The articles below represent the most recent research developments in this rapidly evolving field.

articles.title: Decoding the BRCA2 reversion principles underlying PARP inhibitor resistance
articles.hook: BRCA2 reversion mutations explain PARP inhibitor resistance in breast cancer
articles.summary: Researchers identified how BRCA2 mutations revert to restore function, explaining why some breast cancers develop resistance to PARP inhibitor drugs.

articles.title: Co-occurring rare germline DNA repair gene variants in BRCA1/BRCA2 implicated hereditary breast cancer families.
articles.hook: Rare DNA repair gene variants complicate hereditary breast cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: Researchers found that hereditary breast cancer families carry multiple rare harmful DNA repair gene variants beyond BRCA1/BRCA2, complicating genetic test interpretation.

articles.title: Factors influencing uptake of risk-reducing mastectomy among unaffected Israeli BRCA1/BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers.
articles.hook: Cancer fear and family history drive risk-reducing mastectomy decisions in BRCA carriers
articles.summary: Healthy BRCA gene carriers choosing preventive breast removal are primarily motivated by cancer fear, family history, and support group discussions rather than medical advice.

articles.title: AZD6738 overcomes acquired olaparib resistance in BRCA1 mutation triple-negative breast cancer through down-regulation of BRCA2 and RAD51.
articles.hook: AZD6738 restores olaparib sensitivity in resistant triple-negative breast cancer
articles.summary: AZD6738 combined with olaparib overcomes drug resistance in triple-negative breast cancer by reducing DNA repair proteins.

articles.title: Impaired glucose tolerance in women with BRCA1 versus BRCA2 pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants: Results from a prospective cohort study.
articles.hook: BRCA1 mutations impair glucose tolerance more than BRCA2 variants
articles.summary: Women with BRCA1 mutations show worse glucose tolerance than BRCA2 carriers, possibly due to earlier menopause.

articles.title: A Randomised, Open-Label, Phase III Study of Saruparib (AZD5305) Plus Camizestrant Compared With Physician's Choice CDK4/6 Inhibitor Plus Endocrine Therapy or Plus Camizestrant for the First-Line Treatment of Patients With BRCA1, BRCA2, or PALB2 Mutations and Hormone Receptor Positive, HER2-Negative (IHC 0, 1+, 2+/ ISH Non-amplified) Advanced Breast Cancer (EvoPAR-Breast01)
articles.summary: Study tests saruparib plus camizestrant versus standard therapy for advanced breast cancer in patients with BRCA mutations.

articles.title: Differential sensitivity of MCPH1- and BRCA2-deficient cancer cells to PARP-1 inhibition.
articles.hook: MCPH1-deficient cancer cells show reduced PARP...
articles.summary: MCPH1-deficient cancer cells retain partial DNA repair function and show minimal sensitivity to PARP inhibitors, unlike BRCA2-deficient cells.

articles.title: Investigating the contribution of rare non-coding variants in BRCA1, BRCA2 and PALB2 to hereditary breast cancer.
articles.hook: Rare non-coding variants in BRCA1, BRCA2,...
articles.summary: Rare non-coding variants in BRCA1, BRCA2, and PALB2 genes modestly increase hereditary breast cancer risk, with stronger effects in triple-negative breast cancer.

articles.title: BRCA2-dependent maturation of nascent strands during DNA replication.
articles.hook: BRCA2 enables cancer cells to resist PARP...
articles.summary: BRCA2 protein enables cancer cells to repair DNA damage caused by PARP inhibitor olaparib during replication, suggesting treatment strategies.

articles.title: Combining multiplexed assays of variant effect for enhanced BRCA2 variant classification.
articles.summary: Combining multiple functional tests improved classification accuracy of BRCA2 genetic variants to 98.8%, helping determine cancer risk for thousands of people.
